WHAT WE LEARNED
Attractiveness, feasibility, and execution priority are different decisions
textPreview: Attractiveness, feasibility, and execution priority are different decisions

text: Sources: transition brief; MVP scope; open questions
textPreview: Sources: transition brief; MVP scope; open questions

text: GEOGRAPHY
Attractiveness
Is this market or submarket appealing enough to justify deeper diligence?
textPreview: Is this market or submarket appealing enough to justify deeper diligence?

text: PROPERTY
Feasibility
Can this available property pass mandatory physical, legal, operational, and financial constraints?
textPreview: Can this available property pass mandatory physical, legal, operational, and financial constraints?

text: PORTFOLIO
Execution priority
Given availability, staffing, economics, timing, and dependencies, what should be reviewed first?
textPreview: Given availability, staffing, economics, timing, and dependencies, what should be reviewed first?

text:
The most important learning was that attractiveness, property feasibility, and execution priority are separate decisions. A single hidden score should not combine them.
